agent_authored.description: Cassiopeia reconstructs the developmental history of cells from CRISPR-Cas9 lineage barcodes. Heritable edits accumulate at fixed target sites, so cells that share edits share an ancestor; the package collapses and error-corrects the raw UMI reads into a character matrix, then infers a tree by distance-based (Neighbour-Joining, UPGMA) or greedy/ILP methods, and finally estimates branch lengths under an IID-exponential mutation model with a hand-written log-space forward/backward dynamic program in C++.
evidence: test suite: 485 passed of 521 collected in 54.85s
run with no network namespace: ran_offline=True, downloads_anything=False

modules.title: Bayesian posterior branch-length inference (IIDExponentialBayesian, hand-written C++ log-space forward/backward DP)
entrypoints: cassiopeia.tools.IIDExponentialBayesian(mutation_rate, birth_rate, sampling_probability, discretization_level).estimate_branch_lengths(tree) - the single public call
model.log_joints(node) - available but see hazards; it mixes true -inf, the C++ sentinel -1e16 and O(10) physical values
modules.expensive_path: _InferPosteriorTimes::down() at cassiopeia/tools/branch_length_estimator/_iid_exponential_bayesian_cpp.cpp:124-197 and ::up() at :199-309 - a memoized log-space forward/backward DP over (node v, discretized time t, mutated-character count x), caches down_cache/up_cache shaped [N][T+1][K] as double***, each step combining 3-4 cases through the hand-written logsumexp at :73-84, with posteriors assembled by compute_log_joint() at :308-349. Pure scalar C++, single-threaded, no BLAS, no RNG, no OpenMP; cost O(N*T*K) in both time and memory. Measured through the public Python entrypoint on this host (gcc -O3, complete binary tree from CompleteBinarySimulator + Cas9LineageTracingDataSimulator, K=20 cassettes): 0.19 s at 64 leaves/T=400; 1.17 s at 256 leaves/T=800; 2.08 s at 512 leaves/T=800; 10.38 s at 2048 leaves/T=1200; 20.47 s at 4096 leaves/T=1200. Scaling is linear in N and in T, so a minute-scale acceleration check is reachable at depth 13-14 and real lineage trees (1e4-1e5 cells) run for many minutes. The recursion is over t, so a GPU port is a genuine restructuring job: turn the memoized recursion into an iterative reverse-time sweep over the [T+1][K] plane with the tree traversal as the outer loop.
modules.rationale: This is one module because it is one contract with one owner: a fixed topology plus integer character states plus four scalar model parameters go in, a posterior time distribution per internal node comes out, and every line that computes it - the DP, the logsumexp, the caches, the Cython marshalling and the thin Python driver - lives in this one directory and is written by this package. Nothing in it is delegated: no numpy kernel, no scipy, no BLAS, no external solver, no RNG. It is also the only part of cassiopeia whose numerical core is hand-written C++ rather than numba, which makes the port target unambiguous. Determinism is pinned down by measurement, not assumption: bit-identical log_likelihood, posterior_time and node times across PYTHONHASHSEED in {0, 1, 12345} (sha256 of the float64 buffers matched exactly), and bit-identical between the -O3 pin and a full -O0 rebuild of the extension. There is also a real two-ULP calibration referent, which cassiopeia's integer-only paths lack: perturbing mutation_rate from 0.3 by two ULPs moves log_likelihood by 6.59e-16 relative, the posterior mean node time by 1.21e-16 relative, and posterior_time by 4.75e-15 max relative - small, nonzero, and exactly the kind of spread selfcheck wants as evidence. Suitable official tests counted: 7.
excluded: cassiopeia/tools/branch_length_estimator/IIDExponentialMLE.py (245 lines) and all 33 collected tests in test/tools_tests/branch_length_estimator_tests/iid_exponential_mle_test.py. It is a sibling in the same directory but the numerics belong to cvxpy (the tests are parameterized over ECOS and SCS backends); a solver cannot port code this package does not own, and convex-solver output is not bit-reproducible across builds.

The 3 error-raising tests in the module's own test file (test_small_discretization_level_raises_error, test_invalid_tree_topology_raises_error, test_invalid_sampling_probability_raises_error). They are legitimate official tests but they grade exception type, not physics, so they are breadth candidates rather than pointwise checks.
cassiopeia/tools/fitness_estimator/ including the vendored _jungle subtree - a different tool with a separate third-party copyright.
hazards: model.log_joints(node) is NOT safe to grade pointwise as-is. Measured on the many-characters closed-form fixture at T=200: the 201-element array contains 1 true -inf, 4 entries equal to the C++ sentinel -1e16 (INF in _iid_exponential_bayesian_cpp.h), and finite values in [-21.91, -11.32]. A relative-error rubric over the raw array produces nan. The official test itself dodges this by slicing [50:-50]. Grade posterior_time, log_likelihood and node times (all finite) instead, or mask the non-finite band explicitly.

CassiopeiaTree.set_times at cassiopeia/data/CassiopeiaTree.py:871-877 raises CassiopeiaTreeError('Time of parent greater than that of child') whenever the posterior means come out non-monotone. This is not hypothetical: it fired on depth=8 K=30 T=500, depth=9 K=40 T=800, depth=7 K=30 T=600 and depth=6 K=30 T=1000 in my sweep, while K=20 ran clean at every depth up to 12. The check IC must be a config verified not to raise, and it must be verified for nominal, variant AND altbuild - a port that shifts a near-tied pair by 1e-15 turns a passing check into an uncaught exception rather than a toler

The altbuild floor is zero for this kernel. Rebuilding the extension with -O0 instead of -O3 (build.py line 34) gave byte-identical log_likelihood, log_joints and posterior_time buffers, because the logsumexp is a fixed-order scalar loop with no fastmath and no vectorized reduction. Floor evidence must therefore come from the two-ULP variant (which does move, ~1e-15) and from a compiler swap, not from the optimization level. The tolerance must be argued from physics, not from a measured floor of zero.

Memory is O(N*T*K) doubles across two caches. At 8192 nodes, T=1200, K=21 that is roughly 3.3 GB resident. The container needs headroom, and the acceleration config has to be sized against GPU memory too.

down() and up() are mutually recursive over t with depth ~T. At T=2400 that is 2400 frames deep per call chain; it ran, but a naive GPU port that keeps the recursion will not work and a CPU reference at very large T could hit the stack limit.

_non_root_internal_nodes at IIDExponentialBayesian.py:30 does list(set(...) - set(...)), so node processing order is PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent. I measured that this does not change any numerical output (each node's posterior is independent), but any check that grades an ordered list of nodes rather than a keyed mapping would be flaky. Grade by node name.

The official test tolerances are loose by design (relative error <= 0.01, total variation <= 0.03, decimal=1) because they compare against a coarse numerical quadrature. They are the right tests to derive checks FROM, but their bounds are not usable as rubric bounds - the rubric must be derived from the reference output's own reproducibility.
Investigation verdict for this codebase: GO-WITH-CAVEAT.

modules.title: Pairwise character dissimilarity and distance-based tree solvers (Neighbor-Joining, UPGMA, Shared-Mutation-Joining)
entrypoints: CassiopeiaTree.compute_dissimilarity_map(dissimilarity_function, threads=...) then .get_dissimilarity_map() -> the n x n float DataFrame
cassiopeia.solver.NeighborJoiningSolver(dissimilarity_function=..., add_root=True).solve(tree) -> tree topology + branch lengths, read back via tree.get_newick(record_branch_lengths=True)
cassiopeia.data.utilities.compute_dissimilarity_map(cm, C, dissimilarity_function, weights, missing_state_indicator, threads) - the raw flattened condensed array

cassiopeia.solver.dissimilarity_functions.{weighted_hamming_distance, hamming_distance, hamming_similarity_normalized_over_missing, weighted_hamming_similarity, cluster_dissimilarity, ...} and the prior transformations
excluded: cassiopeia/solver/SpectralNeighborJoiningSolver.py (362) and its 15 tests - line :202 calls scipy.linalg.svd, and cupyx.scipy.sparse.linalg is an analogue for that sub-step, which is exactly the delegation pattern that counts as a twin.

cassiopeia/solver/SpectralSolver.py (186), SpectralGreedySolver.py (215), MaxCutSolver.py (181), MaxCutGreedySolver.py (186) and their tests - MaxCutSolver.py:117 and :139 call np.random.normal with no seed, so the output is not reproducible run to run; SpectralSolver.py:127 calls sp.linalg.eig, whose eigenvector signs and ordering vary across LAPACK builds.
cassiopeia/solver/ILPSolver.py (725) and 5 of its 14 tests - the Steiner-tree solve needs a Gurobi licence, which is unavailable in an offline container (all 5 skip today).

cassiopeia/solver/VanillaGreedySolver.py, GreedySolver.py, PercolationSolver.py, HybridSolver.py - character-splitting rather than distance-based, a different contract, and HybridSolver adds a multiprocessing.Pool over subproblems.
hazards: cassiopeia/data/utilities.py is shared, not exclusively owned: the same file also holds to_newick, lca_characters, the bootstrap helpers and the treedata converter, which belong to no module in this cut. It must be recorded as overlapping_owned, not owned outright.

The numba jit is applied at call time inside a try/except (utilities.py:219-242, SharedMutationJoiningSolver.py:78-97). When numbaization fails - notably for cluster_dissimilarity, which arrives wrapped in a functools.partial and raises TypeError - the code silently falls back to pure Python and emits a CassiopeiaTreeWarning. A check whose IC happens to take that branch would grade the Python fallback, not the kernel, and the acceleration signal would vanish. Any check must assert it took the jitted path.
The ambiguous-character branch at utilities.py:227-233 jits with nopython=False, forceobj=True, parallel=True. That is object mode; a port must not be graded through it.

Neighbor-Joining topology is a discrete output. Near-tied Q values mean an accelerated port can return a different but equally valid tree. A pointwise rubric over the Newick string is brittle; grade the dissimilarity map and the branch-length vector, and treat topology as an invariants-style check (e.g. Robinson-Foulds distance to the reference), not a string compare.

A prior-free check is integer-exact (values are exact k/m rationals, confirmed by measurement), so identical=true will hold for a correct port and the two-ULP variant has no referent - the same limitation flagged on scirpy. Use a prior-weighted IC if a nonzero variant spread is wanted.

The whole solver package is imported through cassiopeia/solver/__init__.py, which imports ILPSolver, which imports the Gurobi-dependent path. Importing the module at all must not require Gurobi (it does not today, but the Dockerfile must not accidentally break the lazy import).
Investigation verdict for this codebase: GO-WITH-CAVEAT.
modules.purpose: One module because it is one pipeline with one data structure: a character matrix becomes a condensed pairwise dissimilarity array, and the three agglomerative solvers all consume exactly that array through the shared DistanceSolver base class, iterating find_cherry , update_dissimilarity_map until the tree is built. Splitting the metric from the solver would leave the metric with no consumer and the solver with no input. It is also the module with the largest official-test surface in the repository and the one whose kernels are plainly data-parallel. Determinism is measured, not assumed: the dissimilarity map and the resulting NJ Newick string were byte-identical across threads in {1, 2, 4} crossed with PYTHONHASHSEED in {0, 7} (sha256 of the float64 matrix and of the branch-length Newick matched in all six runs). That holds because compute_dissimilarity_map's multiprocessing path (utilities.py:243-278) splits the condensed index range into disjoint batches over shared memory and writes each dm[i] independently - there is no reduction to reorder. modules.title: UMI collapse and Hamming-based UMI error correction (owned Cython)
entrypoints: cassiopeia.pp.collapse_umis(bam_fp, output_directory, max_hq_mismatches, max_indels, method, n_threads) -> collapsed molecule DataFrame
cassiopeia.preprocess.collapse_cython.hamming_distance_matrix(seqs) and .register_corrections(ds, max_UMI_distance, UMIs) - the owned kernel seam, called from UMI_utils.py:727-728
modules.expensive_path: collapse_cython.hamming_distance_matrix at cassiopeia/preprocess/collapse_cython.pyx:17-37 - an O(n^2 * L) all-pairs Hamming distance over UMI sequences encoded into a long[:, ::1] memoryview, measured at 15.07 s for n=10000 x L=120 on this host, feeding register_corrections at :39-84. The per-pair helper hamming_distance at :5-15 is the inner loop used by the collapse path in UMI_utils.py. This is genuinely owned compiled code and the n^2 loop is the most obviously GPU-shaped kernel in the repository.
modules.rationale: One module because it is the first stage of the cassiopeia pipeline and it is closed: raw aligned reads in a BAM become a deduplicated, error-corrected molecule table, and every step between those two points - the Hamming matrix, the correction registry, the UMI resolution and the molecule filters - is in these four files. It is semi-independent of the other two modules in the strict sense that it produces the character matrix they consume and shares no code with them. Determinism: the 11 collected tests across collapse_umi_test.py and error_correct_umi_test.py pass identically under PYTHONHASHSEED 0 and 9 (9.52 s and 9.36 s), and the default n_threads is 1, so the graded path is single-threaded. Included mainly so the human sees the third owned-Cython option; I do not recommend packaging it first. Suitable official tests counted: 18.
excluded: cassiopeia/preprocess/alignment_utilities.py and align_sequence_test.py (4 tests) - alignment is delegated to the external pyseq-align library.
convert_fastqs_to_unmapped_bam (5 tests) and filter_bam (1) - pure pysam I/O, no owned numerics.
cassiopeia/preprocess/lineage_utils.py and call_lineage_groups (6 tests), doublet_utils.py - clustering and heuristics rather than a compiled kernel.
hazards: The owned kernel is only reachable through BAM file I/O via pysam. Every official test in this module drives collapse_umis or error_correct_umis over a fixture BAM, so a check's run.sh has to ship and parse binary BAM fixtures, and the graded object is a molecule table (mixed string/int columns) rather than a float array. That is materially harder to write a pointwise rubric for than either of the other two modules.

hamming_distance_matrix is called once per (cellBC, intBC) group, and real groups hold tens of UMIs. The measured 15 s at n=10000 is a synthetic single-call benchmark; at test scale the n^2 work is negligible, so the acceleration check would have to construct an artificial single large group, which is a weaker claim to 'the codebase's own official test'.

The Bayesian collapse variant (test_collapse_bam_bayesian) pulls in a separate probabilistic path in UMI_utils.py that I have not determinism-probed at the value level - only that its test passes reproducibly.
pipeline.py drives joblib and pysam with n_threads; the default is 1 and the tests use the default, but a check must pin n_threads explicitly.
cassiopeia/preprocess/utilities.py (802 lines) is also used by the lineage-group and doublet code that this cut excludes, so it is overlapping_owned rather than owned.
Investigation verdict for this codebase: GO-WITH-CAVEAT.

covers: Bayesian posterior branch-length inference (IIDExponentialBayesian, hand-written C++ log-space forward/backward DP)
known_gaps: model.log_joints(node) is NOT safe to grade pointwise as-is. Measured on the many-characters closed-form fixture at T=200: the 201-element array contains 1 true -inf, 4 entries equal to the C++ sentinel -1e16 (INF in _iid_exponential_bayesian_cpp.h), and finite values in [-21.91, -11.32]. A relative-error rubric over the raw array produces nan. The official test itself dodges this by slicing [50:-50]. Grade posterior_time, log_likelihood and node times (all finite) instead, or mask the non-finite band explicitly.

CassiopeiaTree.set_times at cassiopeia/data/CassiopeiaTree.py:871-877 raises CassiopeiaTreeError('Time of parent greater than that of child') whenever the posterior means come out non-monotone. This is not hypothetical: it fired on depth=8 K=30 T=500, depth=9 K=40 T=800, depth=7 K=30 T=600 and depth=6 K=30 T=1000 in my sweep, while K=20 ran clean at every depth up to 12. The check IC must be a config verified not to raise, and it must be verified for nominal, variant AND altbuild - a port that shifts a near-tied pair by 1e-15 turns a passing check into an uncaught exception rather than a tolerance miss.

The altbuild floor is zero for this kernel. Rebuilding the extension with -O0 instead of -O3 (build.py line 34) gave byte-identical log_likelihood, log_joints and posterior_time buffers, because the logsumexp is a fixed-order scalar loop with no fastmath and no vectorized reduction. Floor evidence must therefore come from the two-ULP variant (which does move, ~1e-15) and from a compiler swap, not from the optimization level. The tolerance must be argued from physics, not from a measured floor of zero.

covers: Pairwise character dissimilarity and distance-based tree solvers (Neighbor-Joining, UPGMA, Shared-Mutation-Joining)
known_gaps: cassiopeia/data/utilities.py is shared, not exclusively owned: the same file also holds to_newick, lca_characters, the bootstrap helpers and the treedata converter, which belong to no module in this cut. It must be recorded as overlapping_owned, not owned outright.

The numba jit is applied at call time inside a try/except (utilities.py:219-242, SharedMutationJoiningSolver.py:78-97). When numbaization fails - notably for cluster_dissimilarity, which arrives wrapped in a functools.partial and raises TypeError - the code silently falls back to pure Python and emits a CassiopeiaTreeWarning. A check whose IC happens to take that branch would grade the Python fallback, not the kernel, and the acceleration signal would vanish. Any check must assert it took the jitted path.
The ambiguous-character branch at utilities.py:227-233 jits with nopython=False, forceobj=True, parallel=True. That is object mode; a port must not be graded through it.

covers: UMI collapse and Hamming-based UMI error correction (owned Cython)
known_gaps: The owned kernel is only reachable through BAM file I/O via pysam. Every official test in this module drives collapse_umis or error_correct_umis over a fixture BAM, so a check's run.sh has to ship and parse binary BAM fixtures, and the graded object is a molecule table (mixed string/int columns) rather than a float array. That is materially harder to write a pointwise rubric for than either of the other two modules.

hamming_distance_matrix is called once per (cellBC, intBC) group, and real groups hold tens of UMIs. The measured 15 s at n=10000 is a synthetic single-call benchmark; at test scale the n^2 work is negligible, so the acceleration check would have to construct an artificial single large group, which is a weaker claim to 'the codebase's own official test'.

The Bayesian collapse variant (test_collapse_bam_bayesian) pulls in a separate probabilistic path in UMI_utils.py that I have not determinism-probed at the value level - only that its test passes reproducibly.
